beats.lead: The 2012 breakthrough that started the deep-learning boom
beats.text: needed millions of images labelled by hand first.
beats.note: AlexNet gets the credit. The dataset it was trained on took human beings years to build.

beats.name: Fei-Fei Li
beats.role: Set out to build a dataset mapping images to the tens of thousands of categories in WordNet — a project other researchers thought was hopeless at that scale.

beats.context: People hired through Amazon Mechanical Turk, across 167 countries, spending nearly two years labelling and cross-checking millions of images.

beats.lead: Some images needed more checking than others
beats.text: A cat might need two opinions. A miniature husky needed ten.
beats.note: The team built statistical models of how individual Turkers behaved just to catch the ones cutting corners or getting it wrong.
First shown as a poster at a computer vision conference in 2009. Three years later, it was the training data behind AlexNet's win — and the moment computer vision changed.

beats.line: The algorithm got the headlines. The dataset made it possible.
